This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 24.06.2017 passed by XII Addl. MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.421/2016 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant/injured, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,44,000/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 Medical bills -Rs.1,04,000/-
 Pain and suffering,special diet  and attendant -Rs.40,000/-
 ------------------
 TOTAL Rs.1,44,000/-
 ==========
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The appellant was in the private employment.
The appellant suffered fracture of right femur bone and doctor has issued PDC of 20%.

Therefore, Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding any sum under the head of permanent disability and future treatment and loss of future prospects, hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the overall facts and totality of the circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant as well as the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the injured assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced.

Accordingly, the compensation amount is recalculated as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.3,000 40% x 10% x 12 x 17 =Rs.85,600/-

Medical bills -Rs.1,04,000/-
 Pain and suffering,special diet  and attendant -Rs.40,000/-
 ------------------
 TOTAL AMOUNT Rs.2,29,600/-
 7 .

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in th Bhupendra vs Ravindra on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59260856/
2 Rs.2,29,600/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.1,44,000/-. Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.85,600/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.85,600/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE RJ Bhupendra vs Ravindra on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59260856/
